name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 233 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 36% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 233 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 36 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Manipur security forces including police, CRPF, BSF, Assam Rifles and the army have launched search operations and hold fortnightly security review meetings after a gunfight in Kangpokpi and a rally in Ukhrul demanding an end to ethnic violence and the SoO pact. In Kashmir a blast at a police outpost in Ghaziabad was claimed by a Kashmir-linked outfit, prompting an ATS probe, while IGP Sujit Kumar noted a single local terrorist remains active. Naxalites in the Bastar Maoist belt dumped 900 detonators and electronic equipment. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Manipur sikkerhetsstyrker, inkludert politi, CRPF, BSF, Assam Rifles og hæren, har igangsatt søkeoperasjoner og holder to-ukentlige sikkerhetsgjennomganger etter en skuddveksling i Kangpokpi og en demonstrasjon i Ukhrul som krever en slutt på etnisk vold og SoO-pakten. I Kashmir ble en eksplosjon ved en politipost i Ghaziabad gjort til ansvar av en Kashmir-tilknyttet gruppe, noe som førte til en ATS-undersøkelse, mens IGP Sujit Kumar bemerket at en enkelt lokal terrorist fortsatt er aktiv. Naxalitter i Bastar-Maoistbeltet kastet 900 detonatorer og elektronisk utstyr. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
